description: Two value comparators in 4HP, each giving all six comparison results, with the lower pair reading the upper pair when left unpatched

inputs.text: The signal passed by any comparison output that comes out true; with the jack empty a true output carries the level set on the menu
The signal passed by any comparison output that comes out false; with the jack empty a false output carries the level set on the menu
One of the two voltages the upper section compares; an empty jack reads 0V
The first voltage the lower section compares; with the jack empty it reads the A input
The second voltage the lower section compares; with the jack empty it reads the B input

outputs.text: Carries the true signal while that section's two voltages are within the tolerance of each other
Carries the true signal while that section's two voltages are further apart than the tolerance
Carries the true signal while the first voltage is greater than the second or within the tolerance of it
Carries the true signal while the first voltage is greater than the second by more than the tolerance
Carries the true signal while the first voltage is less than the second or within the tolerance of it
Carries the true signal while the first voltage is less than the second by more than the tolerance

notes: this module has no knobs at all: the tolerance is a menu setting and there are no offset knobs, so a fixed comparison voltage has to come from another module
patching C and D leaves the lower section independent; leaving them empty makes it compare the same A and B as the upper section, which is only useful with one of them patched
menu: True output level — sets the voltage a true output carries when the True input is empty, 10V unless you change it
False output level — sets the voltage a false output carries when the False input is empty, 0V unless you change it
Tolerance — sets how far apart two values may be while counting as equal, a twenty-fourth of a volt unless you change it
Clipping range — clamps every output to the range chosen, -12V to 12V unless you change it, and Off lets the output run to any voltage
Process quality: Audio, High, Balanced, Low, Very low — sets how often the module runs its algorithm, from every cycle down to every 256th; below Balanced a 1ms trigger can be missed

inputs.0:
polyphonic

unpatched it reads the True output level from the menu.
inputs.1:
polyphonic

unpatched it reads the False output level from the menu.
inputs.4:
polyphonic

unpatched it reads the A input.
inputs.5:
polyphonic

unpatched it reads the B input.
